spec.title: JVM
spec.description: JVM, process, and system metrics, following the OpenTelemetry conventions.

spec.name: instance
spec.label: Instance
spec.description: Application instances, from the most recently started.

spec.title: Uptime
spec.description: Time since the JVM started.

spec.title: Started
spec.description: When the JVM started.

spec.title: Java
spec.description: Java runtime vendor and version.

spec.title: CPUs
spec.description: Processors available to the JVM. In a container, it reflects the CPU limit.

spec.title: Live Threads
spec.description: Platform threads currently alive, daemon threads included.

spec.title: Open Files
spec.description: File descriptors currently open by the process.

spec.title: Process CPU
spec.description: CPU used by the JVM process, relative to the available processors.

spec.title: Heap
spec.description: Heap memory in use, relative to the maximum heap size (-Xmx). It naturally rises and falls with garbage collection: *Heap after GC* shows the trend that matters.

spec.expr: sum(jvm_memory_used_bytes{job="$job", instance="$instance", jvm_memory_type="heap"}) / sum(jvm_memory_limit_bytes{job="$job", instance="$instance", jvm_memory_type="heap"} > 0)

spec.title: GC Overhead
spec.description: Share of time spent in garbage collection pauses over the last five minutes. A steadily high value means the JVM is busy reclaiming memory instead of running the application.

options.content:
**Reading this dashboard**

* **High CPU**: compare *Process CPU* with *GC Overhead*. A large GC share means the JVM is short of memory.
* **Memory leak**: *Heap after GC* climbing steadily or above 70-80%. Growing *Non-Heap* or *Classes* points to a class loader leak.
* **Latency spikes**: *GC Duration* above about 200 ms, or pauses filling a large share of each second.
* **Slow with idle CPU**: *blocked* threads in *Thread States*, waiting on locks.

spec.title: CPU Usage
spec.description: CPU used by the JVM process and by the whole system, relative to the available processors.

spec.title: System Load
spec.description: Runnable tasks queued or running on the system, averaged over one minute. A load steadily above the number of CPUs means the system is saturated. Not available on Windows.

spec.title: Heap
spec.description: Memory where the application objects live. The JVM can use up to *max* (in the legend), has *committed* what is reserved from the operating system, and *used* is occupied by objects.

spec.title: Non-Heap
spec.description: Memory managed by the JVM outside the heap: class metadata (Metaspace) and compiled code (Code Cache). Metaspace is unbounded by default, so there is no overall max. Metaspace that keeps growing points to a class loader leak, for example classes retained across restarts.

spec.title: Heap after GC
spec.description: Heap memory in use right after the last garbage collection, per pool. The old generation value is the memory the application really retains: a value that keeps growing points to a memory leak.

spec.title: $heap_pool
spec.description: Memory pool of the JVM. The pools depend on the garbage collector in use. *Eden*: new objects. *Survivor*: objects that survived a young collection. *Old Gen*: long-lived objects. *Metaspace*: class metadata, including *Compressed Class Space*. *CodeCache*: JIT-compiled code.

spec.title: $nonheap_pool
spec.description: Memory pool of the JVM. The pools depend on the garbage collector in use. *Eden*: new objects. *Survivor*: objects that survived a young collection. *Old Gen*: long-lived objects. *Metaspace*: class metadata, including *Compressed Class Space*. *CodeCache*: JIT-compiled code.

spec.title: GC Time
spec.description: Share of time spent in garbage collection, per collector. It includes the concurrent phases that run alongside the application (such as G1 Concurrent GC or ZGC Cycles), so only part of it pauses the application.

spec.title: GC Duration
spec.description: Average and longest garbage collection, concurrent phases included. Long pauses delay every request in progress. G1, the default collector, aims for pauses under 200 ms (-XX:MaxGCPauseMillis).

spec.expr: sum by (jvm_gc_name) (rate(jvm_gc_duration_seconds_sum{job="$job", instance="$instance"}[$__rate_interval])) / sum by (jvm_gc_name) (rate(jvm_gc_duration_seconds_count{job="$job", instance="$instance"}[$__rate_interval]))

spec.title: Collections
spec.description: Garbage collections per second, by action and cause.

spec.title: Allocation and Promotion
spec.description: Rate at which the application allocates objects in the young generation, and at which surviving objects are promoted to the old generation. High promotion fills the old generation and leads to costlier collections.

spec.title: Threads
spec.description: Platform threads alive, of which daemon threads, and the highest count since the JVM started.

spec.title: Thread States
spec.description: Platform threads by state. Many *blocked* threads indicate contention on locks.

spec.title: Virtual Threads
spec.description: Virtual threads running on a carrier thread (mounted) or waiting for one (queued), and the carrier threads started by the scheduler. Requires Java 24 or later.

spec.title: Classes
spec.description: Classes currently loaded, and classes unloaded per second. A count that never stops growing can reveal a class loader leak.

spec.title: Buffer Pools
spec.description: Memory used by direct buffers (native memory for I/O) and mapped buffers (memory-mapped files), outside the heap.
